---
title: "Filter"
subtitle: "Keep rows that match a condition"
---

::: {.sas-equiv}
**SAS:** `WHERE`, subsetting `IF`
:::

`dplyr::filter()` keeps rows for which the condition is `TRUE`.

## Quick reference

{{< include _quickref/filter.md >}}

Worked examples below.

## One condition

```{r}
#| label: one
library(dplyr)

vs <- data.frame(
  USUBJID = c("STD-001-0001", "STD-001-0001", "STD-001-0002"),
  PARAMCD = c("SYSBP", "DIABP", "SYSBP"),
  AVAL = c(120, 80, NA_real_)
)

vs |>
  filter(PARAMCD == "SYSBP")
```

SAS: `where paramcd = "SYSBP";`

## Several conditions

```{r}
#| label: several
vs |>
  filter(PARAMCD == "SYSBP", !is.na(AVAL))
```

Commas in `filter()` mean AND. Use `|` for OR.

::: {.callout-important}
## `NA` in the condition drops the row

`filter(AVAL > 100)` drops rows where `AVAL` is `NA`, because `NA > 100` is not
`TRUE`. Keep missing values on purpose with `is.na(AVAL) | AVAL > 100` when that
is the rule.
:::
